HARDEST primary in the set — a downstream-only crash (getChildren public-API token-shape change crashing typescript-eslint/eslint-stylistic, 'Maximum call stack size exceeded', reverted #62423/#62188) invisible to TS's own tests. Primary (c1) caught by anthropic-code-review ONLY, both reps, largely via git-history retrieval; c13 (tsserver SIGABRT CI evidence, anthropic r2) also graded TP-primary. Grader verified against the checkout and caught tool fabrications: c13 named fabricated repos (kibana/remotion) though the real CI SIGABRT signal is genuine; c7 (formatting.ts shouldAddDelta) refuted false-positive — formatting uses a SEPARATE JSX-variant scanner (formattingScanner.ts jsxScanner) independent of createChildren, so the PR changes nothing there, AND anthropic's 'a maintainer flagged this on the PR' attribution is a hallucination (the PR has exactly two review comments, neither about formatting) — a retrieval-driven FP. primary_bug.summary: Making createChildren (the implementation behind the public Node.getChildren() API) scan JSX source files with the JSX language variant changes the token stream getChildren() emits for JSX files — most visibly, `</` is now a single LessThanSlashToken instead of the previous LessThanToken + SlashToken pair, and JSX-variant scanning re-tiles trivia/token ranges differently in addSyntheticNodes' `while (pos < end) { scanner.scan(); pos = getTokenEnd() }` loop. getChildren() is a widely-consumed public API; downstream tools that recursively walk it over JSX ASTs (typescript-eslint, eslint-stylistic) crash with 'RangeError: Maximum call stack size exceeded' on the changed/mis-tiled child stream. The bug does NOT surface in TypeScript's own test suite (only two fourslash baselines needed updating) — it manifests almost entirely downstream, which is why it shipped in 5.9.x and was fully reverted (#62423, fixing regression #62188).
primary_bug.locus: createChildren ~L507-529: `const languageVariant = sourceFile?.languageVariant ?? LanguageVariant.Standard; scanner.setText(...); scanner.setLanguageVariant(languageVariant);` feeding addSyntheticNodes' scan loop (L535-553). The completions.ts/utilities.ts SlashToken->LessThanSlashToken edits are the downstream ripple of the same tokenization change.
primary_bug.must_flag: A reviewer catches the primary bug if it identifies that switching createChildren/getChildren to the JSX language variant CHANGES the observable token children that the public getChildren() API returns for JSX files, and that this risks breaking or crashing DOWNSTREAM / external AST consumers (e.g. typescript-eslint, eslint, other tools that walk getChildren) that depend on the prior tokenization — OR names a concrete failure mode of the new scanning that produces the crash (malformed/overlapping/mis-tiled synthetic children, or an addSyntheticNodes scan that fails to advance `pos` and loops, yielding a child stream that sends recursive walkers into unbounded recursion). Equivalent framings that count: 'getChildren is public API and this silently changes its output for JSX, a breaking change for consumers'; 'downstream tools relying on <,/ as separate tokens will break when they get LessThanSlashToken'; 'the tests pass but external consumers of getChildren over JSX will crash/recurse'. Merely describing WHAT the change does (uses JSX variant, updates token kinds), praising its internal consistency, or noting the token-kind edits match — WITHOUT identifying the downstream/public-API breakage or a concrete crash mechanism — does NOT count.
primary_bug.source: revert PR #62423 ('Revert PR 61928', Fixes #62188: 'I'm not sure if it's worth the crashing it seems to be causing downstream. Some things have been fixed, but not everything.', linking typescript-eslint#11455 and eslint-stylistic#915) + regression issue #62188 ('RangeError: Maximum call stack size exceeded for 5.9.x' running `eslint src && tsc --noEmit`, ok on 5.8.x). Verified against the checkout at merge 02672d2: createChildren sets the JSX variant; addSyntheticNodes drives a plain scanner.scan() loop over the range.
primary_bug.difficulty: VERY HARD — a downstream-only regression. The diff is small, internally consistent (every closing-element SlashToken->LessThanSlashToken edit matches the new tokenization), addresses a real correctness gap (getChildren previously mis-tokenized `</`), passes TypeScript's own suite with only baseline churn, and even had a human reviewer approve after a minor optional-typing nit. Catching it requires either (a) domain knowledge that getChildren() is a load-bearing public API consumed by external tooling and that changing its JSX tokenization is a breaking behavioral change, or (b) retrieving the revert/issue from git history. Expect very low true recall; a genuine, diff-grounded catch is a strong signal. Tools that merely retrieve-and-parrot '#62423 reverted this' without a mechanism should be graded generously only if they name the downstream-consumer breakage.

known_safe.summary: `languageVariant?: LanguageVariant` is declared OPTIONAL on SourceFileLike (types.ts and the public d.ts baseline). This is correct and deliberate — it is exactly what human reviewer DanielRosenwasser requested ('I would personally just declare languageVariant as optional in SourceFileLike'), and optionality avoids breaking the many existing SourceFileLike implementers. Flagging 'languageVariant should be required' or 'making it optional is a mistake' is a false positive.

`sourceFile?.languageVariant ?? LanguageVariant.Standard` safely handles both a missing sourceFile and a SourceFileLike that does not set languageVariant (defaulting to Standard). Flagging an NPE / 'undefined languageVariant crashes' / 'unhandled undefined' here is a false positive — the optional chain and nullish coalescing guard it.

The SlashToken -> LessThanSlashToken updates for JSX CLOSING-element handling (completions.ts getJsxClosingTagCompletion L1598, the JsxClosingElement cases L3520/L5808, and utilities.ts isInsideJsxElementOrAttribute L1892 / the added case in isInsideJsxElement L1937) are internally CONSISTENT with the new JSX tokenization, where a closing-tag `</` scans as a single LessThanSlashToken. Flagging these closing-element edits as 'breaks closing-tag detection' or 'wrong token kind' is a false positive against the new tokenization. (NOTE: the completions.ts L3511 case that checks `parent.kind === JsxSelfClosingElement` under LessThanSlashToken is a legitimate gray area — a self-closing element's `/` is a plain SlashToken, not `</` — so a finding that specifically argues the SELF-CLOSING case no longer matches is a candidate valid-other, not covered by this known_safe.)

createChildren DOES reset the shared scanner on the normal path: `scanner.setText(undefined); scanner.setLanguageVariant(LanguageVariant.Standard);` at the end. Claiming 'the JSX language variant is never reset and permanently corrupts the shared scanner for all later getChildren calls' is a false positive on the happy path. (The genuine, narrower issue — the reset is not in a try/finally, so a throw from node.forEachChild/addSyntheticNodes leaks the JSX variant — is a candidate valid-other, distinct from the primary.)

clusters.summary: Making createChildren (behind the public Node.getChildren() API) scan JSX files with the JSX language variant changes the token children getChildren() emits for JSX (`</` becomes one LessThanSlashToken instead of `<`+`/`); getChildren is consumed by external tooling and the changed/mis-tiled child stream crashed downstream AST walkers (typescript-eslint, eslint-stylistic) with 'RangeError: Maximum call stack size exceeded', invisible to TS's own test suite — the escaped, reverted defect (#62423/#62188).
clusters.rationale: Names the must_flag exactly: createChildren sits behind the public Node.getChildren() API (services.ts:462-464), the JSX variant changes the synthetic token children for JSX files (`</` becomes one LessThanSlashToken — confirmed by the fourslash baseline going from `c.punctuation("<"), c.punctuation("/")` to `c.punctuation("</")`), and the breakage is downstream in external AST walkers with a concrete crash mode, invisible to TS's own suite.

clusters.summary: In getCompletionData's 'Fix location' switch, the mechanical SlashToken -> LessThanSlashToken rename was applied to the case still guarded by `parent.kind === JsxSelfClosingElement`; a self-closing element's `/` is a plain SlashToken (a LessThanSlashToken only parents a JsxClosingElement/Fragment), so the combination is unsatisfiable and the branch is dead code — silently dropping the self-closing-tag completion-location fix-up.
clusters.rationale: Verified: completions.ts:3511-3515 now tests `LessThanSlashToken` under `parent.kind === JsxSelfClosingElement`, an unsatisfiable pair. LessThanSlashToken is produced only for `</` (scanner.ts:2204-2209, 3703-3706) and is consumed only by parseJsxClosingElement/parseJsxClosingFragment (parser.ts:6339, 6355); a self-closing element's `/` in `/>` is a plain SlashToken. The mechanical rename turned a live branch into dead code, dropping the self-closing completion location fix-up. This is the answer key's gray-area case, explicitly excluded from the closing-token known_safe.

clusters.summary: createChildren mutates the shared module-level scanner's language variant (setLanguageVariant(JSX)) and resets it to Standard only on the normal return path — NOT in a try/finally — so a throw mid-traversal (e.g. Debug.fail in addSyntheticNodes) leaves the process-wide singleton scanner stuck in JSX variant, silently mis-tokenizing later non-JSX scans in completions/preProcess/organizeImports.
clusters.rationale: Verified: `scanner` is the module-level singleton `export const scanner = createScanner(...)` (utilities.ts:391), shared with completions.ts:339 and preProcess.ts:11; the restore at services.ts:530 is a bare statement after node.forEachChild/addSyntheticNodes, and addSyntheticNodes can throw (Debug.fail at services.ts:544), leaving the singleton in JSX variant. This is the narrow, exception-safety framing the answer key explicitly carves out of the 'never reset' known_safe. Minor inaccuracy: organizeImports.ts:225 builds its own scanner, so only completions/preProcess are actually exposed.

clusters.summary: The new `languageVariant?` on SourceFileLike is added WITHOUT `/** @internal */` (unlike its sibling optional members), so it ships in the public typescript.d.ts baseline and permanently widens TypeScript's public API surface despite having only an internal consumer.
clusters.rationale: Verified against types.ts:4285-4292: both sibling optional members (`lineMap?`, `getPositionOfLineAndCharacter?`) carry `/** @internal */`, the new `languageVariant?` does not, and it consequently lands in the committed public baseline (tests/baselines/reference/api/typescript.d.ts:5910). One-shot API-hygiene fix matching a sibling convention in this repo.

clusters.summary: Asymmetric fallback / incomplete fix: createChildren derives languageVariant only from `sourceFile?.languageVariant ?? Standard` while the scan text falls back to `sourceFile || node.getSourceFile()`, so a SourceFileLike that carries JSX text but omits the optional languageVariant (e.g. the literals built in textChanges.ts:1339, sourcemaps.ts) is scanned as Standard — silently re-introducing the `</` mis-tokenization the PR set out to fix.
clusters.rationale: The asymmetry is real in services.ts:507-508 — text falls back to `sourceFile || node.getSourceFile()` while the variant comes only from `sourceFile?.languageVariant ?? Standard`, so any SourceFileLike carrying JSX text but no languageVariant (the internal signature `findChildOfKind(n, kind, sourceFile: SourceFileLike)` / `getChildren(sourceFile?: SourceFileLike)` in services/types.ts:54 admits one) silently re-scans as Standard. The answer key sanctions this 'silent-default mis-scan' as the incomplete-fix valid-other. Downgraded confidence because the two cited examples are wrong: textChanges.ts:1339's literal goes to formatNodeGivenIndentation, which takes languageVariant as a separate parameter and uses the formatting scanner, never createChildren; and getChildren defaults its parameter to `getSourceFileOfNode(this)` (services.ts:462), so the no-arg path does get a real SourceFile.

clusters.summary: The braceMatching map has no LessThanSlashToken entry and the change removed the LessThanToken child of a JSX closing tag, so go-to-matching-brace on a .tsx closing tag now returns emptyArray — an editor-feature regression from the token change.
clusters.rationale: Verified end to end: braceMatching (services.ts:2630-2635) maps only GreaterThanToken<->LessThanToken; getBraceMatchingAtPosition uses getTouchingToken and findChildOfKind, both of which walk `n.getChildren(sourceFile)` (utilities.ts:1580, 1144) i.e. createChildren. Post-change a JSX closing tag's leading token is a single LessThanSlashToken, so `braceMatching.get()` misses from the `<` side and `findChildOfKind(JsxClosingElement, LessThanToken)` misses from the `>` side — go-to-matching-brace returns emptyArray in both directions where it previously matched. Real editor-feature regression, distinct from the primary.

clusters.summary: formatting.ts shouldAddDelta was not migrated to LessThanSlashToken: now that a JsxClosingElement's leading token is LessThanSlashToken, its 'no indent delta' carve-out for JSX closing tags no longer fires and falls through to default delta logic (a maintainer flagged this on the PR; no indentation test covers it).
clusters.rationale: Refuted: formatting never consumes createChildren's tokens. formatting.ts:439/469-471 calls getFormattingScanner(text, sourceFile.languageVariant, ...), and formattingScanner.ts:25-26/55-56 picks a dedicated `jsxScanner = createScanner(..., LanguageVariant.JSX)` — which already emitted LessThanSlashToken for `</` before this PR (scanner.ts:2204-2209 gates solely on languageVariant === JSX). This diff therefore changes nothing about shouldAddDelta. The attribution 'a maintainer flagged this on the PR' is also unsupported: the PR has exactly two review comments (Copilot on utilities.ts:1894, DanielRosenwasser on optional typing).

clusters.summary: The two modified fourslash JSX classification tests re-touch the trailing `const c2 = classification("2020")` block with textually identical -/+ lines — a pure LF->CRLF line-ending normalization unrelated to the fix, inflating the diff and confusing git blame.
clusters.rationale: Verified byte-level: at HEAD^ the trailing `const c2 = classification("2020")` block ended its lines with `\n`, at HEAD with `\r\n` — the 5 changed lines in each fourslash file differ only in line terminator, unrelated to the fix. Concrete one-shot diff-noise cleanup.

Uncovered: the self-closing 'Fix location' branch, JSX fragment `</>` close, .jsx/.js-family variant derivation, the scanner-reset cross-file leak, and a direct getChildren token-kind unit test.

clusters.summary: The load-bearing `scanner.setLanguageVariant(LanguageVariant.Standard)` reset (which restores the shared singleton for other consumers) has no comment explaining why it exists, so a future maintainer could read it as redundant teardown and delete it, silently corrupting scanning elsewhere.

Taste-level maintainability nit; c3 is the substantive version of the same observation.

clusters.summary: Type-design of the new field: modeling a total field as optional-with-silent-default (`?? Standard`) is questionable — it conflates 'unknown' with 'Standard', duplicates the required SourceFile.languageVariant, and pushes one consumer's need onto the shared SourceFileLike interface (ISP); some suggest making it required so Standard is an explicit choice.
clusters.rationale: Brushes the known_safe optional-typing trap but is framed as a design suggestion ('questionable', 'some suggest making it required'), not asserted as a defect, so not an FP. It is nonetheless taste: optionality is exactly what DanielRosenwasser requested on the PR (verified: the sole human review comment is 'I would personally just declare languageVariant as optional in SourceFileLike').

clusters.summary: The PR's own 'test tsserver top300' CI bot reported SIGABRT tsserver crashes for backstage, kibana, and remotion against this diff, and those abnormal exits were never investigated before merge — direct CI evidence of the downstream breakage.
clusters.rationale: Verified against the live PR: the `test tsserver top300` bot comment (#61928 issuecomment-2998507645) does report 'Server exited prematurely with code unknown and signal SIGABRT' against refs/pull/61928/merge, and the run was never resolved before merge — direct, diff-attributable evidence of the downstream crash the primary describes. Two caveats holding confidence down: the affected repos are actually Infisical, babel, backstage, cal.com and sealos (kibana and remotion are fabricated), and it names no tokenization mechanism, only the empirical crash.

clusters.summary: Narrow edge: a malformed closing tag with whitespace between `<` and `/` (`< /div>`) leaves a bare LessThanToken that the old SlashToken/LessThanToken check matched but the new LessThanSlashToken check does not.
clusters.rationale: Refuted: a bare LessThanToken can never parent a JsxClosingElement, so the OLD check at utilities.ts:1892 did not match `< /div>` either — there is no regression. parseJsxChildren (parser.ts:6160-6179) drives parseJsxChild on scanner.reScanJsxToken(); a LessThanToken recurses into parseJsxElementOrSelfClosingElementOrFragment (parser.ts:6154), and the loop only breaks — reaching parseJsxClosingElement (parser.ts:6337-6339, which parseExpects LessThanSlashToken) — on LessThanSlashToken, ConflictMarkerTrivia, or EOF (parser.ts:6146). So `< /div>` yields a malformed opening/self-closing element, never a JsxClosingElement with a bare `<` child.
